{{Current events|year=2023|month=02|day=3|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Tigray War]]
**[[Tigrayan peace process]]
***[[Prime Minister of Ethiopia|Ethiopian prime minister]] [[Abiy Ahmed]] meets with officials of the [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]] for the first time since the signing of a [[Ethiopia–Tigray peace agreement|peace treaty]] in November. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20230203-ethiopia-pm-holds-first-meeting-with-tigray-leaders-since-peace-deal (AFP via RFI)]

'''Business and economy'''
*The [[FTSE 100 Index]], the main [[Stock market index|share index]] of the 100 most highly [[Market capitalization|capitalized]] companies listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]], reaches a record [[Day trading|intraday]] value of 7,906.58 points, surpassing the previous highest intraday value of 7,903.50 points recorded on May 22, 2018. [https://www.barrons.com/news/london-ftse-hits-record-high-above-7-906-points-01675440908 (AFP via ''Barron's'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Chile wildfires]]
**[[Chile]] expands its [[state of emergency]] due to [[wildfires]] that have killed at least 23 people and burned up to 8,000 [[hectare]]s and also declares a catastrophe in the [[Biobío Region|Biobío region]] amid a summer [[heat wave]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/firefighters-battle-dozens-wildfires-chile-emergency-extended-2023-02-04/ (Reuters)]
*Three people are killed and several others are injured when a bus overturns near [[Murska Sobota]], [[Prekmurje]], [[Slovenia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/automotive-accidents-slovenia-6909dc0ababbfe88d63f087e4ef042cf (AP)]
*At least seventeen people are killed in a [[head-on collision]] between a bus and a truck in [[Kohat District]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/automotive-accidents-pakistan-e9178fa92ac831e05185e8159b514428 (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2023 China balloon incident]]
**[[China–United States relations]]
***The [[United States]] accuses [[China]] of "a clear violation of sovereignty" after a suspected meteorological [[high altitude balloon]] is noted hovering over [[Montana]]. [[U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Antony Blinken]] postpones his [[List of international trips made by Antony Blinken as United States Secretary of State|official visit]] to [[Beijing]], initially scheduled for February 5, in response to the incident. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/chinese-spy-balloon-montana-pentagon-b2275253.html (''The Independent'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2023/feb/03/china-spy-balloon-secretary-of-state-trip-postponed (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/2/3/blinken-postpones-visit-to-china-because-of-balloon-incident (Al Jazeera)]
***The [[United States Department of Defense]] reports that a second [[high altitude balloon]] has been discovered flying over [[Latin America]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/national-security/chinese-balloon-cause-civilian-injuries-deaths-rcna69052 (NBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Corruption in South Korea]]
**A court in [[South Korea]] [[sentence (law)|sentences]] former [[Ministry of Justice (South Korea)|justice minister]] [[Cho Kuk]] to two years in prison after [[conviction|convicting]] him on [[criminal charge|charges]] of abuse of power and for helping his children enter prestigious schools using fake credentials. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/s-korean-court-sentences-ex-minister-to-2-years-in-prison/2023/02/03/b8928bbe-a396-11ed-8b47-9863fda8e494_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*The [[Brazilian Navy]] [[scuttles]] the [[Ship commissioning|decommissioned]] [[Brazilian aircraft carrier São Paulo|aircraft carrier ''São Paulo'']] into the [[Atlantic Ocean]], following the rejections of [[injunction]]s from the [[Ministry of the Environment (Brazil)|Ministry of the Environment]] and the [[Federal Public Ministry]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20230204-brazil-scuttles-warship-in-atlantic-despite-pollution-concerns (AFP via RFI)]
